spec.goal: Build the two-day program of the conference from the talk submissions and the speakers' emails. Place every talk on the rooms x slots grid of one day, in its own track, with no room or speaker double-booked, every speaker available at their slot, every room big enough for its expected audience, and never two talks of one track at the same time. Honor the speakers' time preferences where possible, and write a short blurb per session.

root_goal.goal: Build the two-day program of the conference from the talk submissions and the speakers' emails. Place every talk on the rooms x slots grid of one day, in its own track, with no room or speaker double-booked, every speaker available at their slot, every room big enough for its expected audience, and never two talks of one track at the same time. Honor the speakers' time preferences where possible, and write a short blurb per session.

abstracts.abstract: This talk walks through how our team approached data lineage over the past year. No prior experience is needed, but familiarity with the basics helps. Organizers of past editions told us to plan for around 146 people.
abstracts.speaker: Elif Fischer
abstracts.title: Scaling data lineage for small teams

abstracts.abstract: We share the mistakes we made with lakehouse tables and how we fixed them. No prior experience is needed, but familiarity with the basics helps. Organizers of past editions told us to plan for around 36 people.
abstracts.speaker: Olga Sato
abstracts.title: A practical guide to lakehouse tables

abstracts.abstract: Why data contracts is harder than it looks, and a design that holds up. The session ends with a checklist attendees can apply on Monday. Last year a similar session drew roughly 50 people.
abstracts.speaker: Rosa Iyer
abstracts.title: Lessons from data contracts in production

abstracts.abstract: A hands-on look at query optimization, with code and real measurements. We compare three approaches and explain the trade-offs we accepted. Last year a similar session drew roughly 39 people.
abstracts.speaker: Pablo Haddad
abstracts.title: A practical guide to query optimization

abstracts.abstract: This talk walks through how our team approached columnar storage over the past year. We compare three approaches and explain the trade-offs we accepted. Expected audience: about 73 participants.
abstracts.speaker: Yusuf Kowalski
abstracts.title: A practical guide to columnar storage

abstracts.abstract: Why vector databases is harder than it looks, and a design that holds up. Expect concrete numbers, a few failure stories and an open-source companion repo. Organizers of past editions told us to plan for around 54 people.
abstracts.speaker: Carmen Novak
abstracts.title: Vector databases: what actually worked

abstracts.abstract: A hands-on look at lakehouse tables, with code and real measurements. No prior experience is needed, but familiarity with the basics helps. We expect around 44 attendees.
abstracts.speaker: Hiro Sato
abstracts.title: Lakehouse tables without the hype

abstracts.abstract: We share the mistakes we made with event sourcing and how we fixed them. Expect concrete numbers, a few failure stories and an open-source companion repo. Last year a similar session drew roughly 65 people.
abstracts.speaker: Olga Fischer
abstracts.title: Scaling event sourcing for small teams

abstracts.abstract: Why trust in AI assistants is harder than it looks, and a design that holds up. We compare three approaches and explain the trade-offs we accepted. Organizers of past editions told us to plan for around 59 people.
abstracts.speaker: Lars Sato
abstracts.title: A practical guide to trust in AI assistants

abstracts.abstract: This talk walks through how our team approached visualizing uncertainty over the past year. The session ends with a checklist attendees can apply on Monday. Organizers of past editions told us to plan for around 56 people.
abstracts.speaker: Chen Okafor
abstracts.title: Visualizing uncertainty: what actually worked

abstracts.abstract: A hands-on look at inclusive language tools, with code and real measurements. We compare three approaches and explain the trade-offs we accepted. Organizers of past editions told us to plan for around 62 people.
abstracts.speaker: Wen Moreau
abstracts.title: Scaling inclusive language tools for small teams

abstracts.abstract: Why developer experience is harder than it looks, and a design that holds up. Expect concrete numbers, a few failure stories and an open-source companion repo. We expect around 20 attendees.
abstracts.speaker: Jonas Moreau
abstracts.title: Rethinking developer experience

abstracts.abstract: A hands-on look at explainable recommendations, with code and real measurements. The session ends with a checklist attendees can apply on Monday. Expected audience: about 48 participants.
abstracts.speaker: Ana Silva
abstracts.title: A practical guide to explainable recommendations

abstracts.abstract: This talk walks through how our team approached collaborative editing over the past year. We compare three approaches and explain the trade-offs we accepted. Organizers of past editions told us to plan for around 74 people.
abstracts.speaker: Dara Petrov
abstracts.title: Collaborative editing without the hype

abstracts.abstract: This talk walks through how our team approached onboarding design over the past year. Expect concrete numbers, a few failure stories and an open-source companion repo. Last year a similar session drew roughly 192 people.
abstracts.speaker: Lars Sato
abstracts.title: Scaling onboarding design for small teams

abstracts.abstract: We share the mistakes we made with usability testing at scale and how we fixed them. The session ends with a checklist attendees can apply on Monday. Organizers of past editions told us to plan for around 85 people.
abstracts.speaker: Yusuf Kowalski
abstracts.title: Lessons from usability testing at scale in production

abstracts.abstract: This talk walks through how our team approached multi-agent planning over the past year. We compare three approaches and explain the trade-offs we accepted. We expect around 104 attendees.
abstracts.speaker: Lars Iyer
abstracts.title: Multi-agent planning without the hype

abstracts.abstract: We share the mistakes we made with long-context attention and how we fixed them. We compare three approaches and explain the trade-offs we accepted. Last year a similar session drew roughly 54 people.
abstracts.speaker: Pablo Byrne
abstracts.title: Long-context attention: what actually worked

abstracts.abstract: Why LLM evaluation harnesses is harder than it looks, and a design that holds up. We compare three approaches and explain the trade-offs we accepted. Last year a similar session drew roughly 193 people.
abstracts.speaker: Ximena Silva
abstracts.title: Scaling LLM evaluation harnesses for small teams

abstracts.abstract: We share the mistakes we made with quantized inference and how we fixed them. No prior experience is needed, but familiarity with the basics helps. Expected audience: about 30 participants.
abstracts.speaker: Elif Fischer
abstracts.title: Scaling quantized inference for small teams

abstracts.abstract: Why retrieval-augmented generation is harder than it looks, and a design that holds up. We compare three approaches and explain the trade-offs we accepted. Last year a similar session drew roughly 22 people.
abstracts.speaker: Zoe Haddad
abstracts.title: Retrieval-augmented generation: what actually worked

abstracts.abstract: We share the mistakes we made with agent tool use and how we fixed them. No prior experience is needed, but familiarity with the basics helps. We expect around 46 attendees.
abstracts.speaker: Wen Sato
abstracts.title: Agent tool use: what actually worked

abstracts.abstract: A hands-on look at prompt caching, with code and real measurements. The session ends with a checklist attendees can apply on Monday. Expected audience: about 54 participants.
abstracts.speaker: Yusuf Tanaka
abstracts.title: Scaling prompt caching for small teams

abstracts.abstract: A hands-on look at model distillation, with code and real measurements. Expect concrete numbers, a few failure stories and an open-source companion repo. We expect around 199 attendees.
abstracts.speaker: Dara Petrov
abstracts.title: Lessons from model distillation in production

abstracts.speaker: Kemi Silva

abstracts.abstract: We share the mistakes we made with reward modelling and how we fixed them. The session ends with a checklist attendees can apply on Monday. Expected audience: about 70 participants.
